audit.whatIsWrong: mid states "her R1 knocks you airborne from range".
audit.why: Perfect Execution R1 is a leap that damages enemies struck — it applies no knockup and carries no CC flag at all. A player told to expect an airborne will read the wrong tell and mistime their answer.
audit.corrected: R1 leaps to you from 675 range with no displacement; the leap itself is the tell, and R2 is the execute.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json (R: "Akali leaps in a direction, damaging enemies she strikes"; flags: dash, execute — no hardCC/knockup)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Twilight Shroud makes Devour uncastable. wants.foe[0] only claims the shroud makes a Q-stun "fire into empty shroud".
audit.why: Devour is a point-and-click cast, and inside the shroud Akali is "unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks". Against every other matchup Devour is your answer to a committed dive; against Akali it is simply greyed out while she sits in W. That is the defining interaction of the lane and it was absent.
audit.corrected: Hold your 3 stacks until she leaves the shroud — Devour will not cast on her inside it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json (W: "unable to be selected by enemy spells and attacks")
League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — Devour cast range 250, requires 3 stacks

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3], whys[6], wants.you[0], tradeGood, breakdown.trading and dosFull all describe a "Q-stun into Devour" / "empowered Q-stun into Devour" pattern.
audit.why: Tongue Lash at 3 stacks stuns and consumes all three stacks; Devour requires 3 stacks and consumes them. The combo does not exist — three stacks buys the stun or the eat.
audit.corrected: Against Akali the eat is the correct spend, since the stun does nothing about her shroud reset.
sources: League of Legends Wiki — Tahm Kench (wiki.leagueoflegends.com/en-us/Tahm_Kench) — "All three An Acquired Taste stacks will be consumed even if Tongue Lash's stun is negated"

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry never mentions that Shuriken Flip can mark Akali's own smoke cloud.
audit.why: Riot's own text: "The first enemy or smoke cloud hit is marked. Re-cast to dash to the marked target." She can E her own shroud to dash straight back into it, which is how she resets a failed all-in. A Tahm Kench who thinks she is committed will spend stacks on a target that is about to become unselectable again.
audit.corrected: Her E can mark the shroud itself, so leaving W does not mean she is committed — she can flip back in.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json (E: "The first enemy or smoke cloud hit is marked")

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[2] says to activate Thick Skin "the moment Akali commits her E dash", i.e. before her damage lands.
audit.why: Thick Skin converts damage ALREADY stored into a shield. Popping it on an empty grey-health bank produces a near-zero shield and wastes the conversion. The shield is only worth what you have already eaten.
audit.corrected: Take the front half of her combo first, then convert. mid already had this right ("only hit E to shield when she commits a full combo"); wants.you[2] contradicted it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json (E: "Passive: stores a percent of the damage he takes... Active: Convert all stored damage into a temporary shield")

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns names Twilight Shroud as "matchup-defining" but gives no duration or cooldown, so the window is unsizeable.
audit.why: Twilight Shroud is 20s at rank 1 falling to 16s at rank 5; Shuriken Flip is 16s at rank 1; Perfect Execution is 120/90/60. Her Q is energy-gated rather than cooldown-gated — 1.5s cooldown but 110 energy at rank 1, which is what actually limits her early poke.
audit.corrected: Real numbers inserted, and the early-game limiter named correctly as her energy pool rather than a cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: early says Akali can "five-ring you with her passive".
audit.why: This conflates two abilities. Assassin's Mark is the passive: spell damage draws a ring around the target, and Akali empowers her next attack by EXITING that ring. Five Point Strike is her Q. The actionable detail — that she must leave the ring to get the empowered attack — is lost by merging them.
audit.corrected: Named separately, with the ring exit given as the tell.
sources: champ-data/_kits/akali.json (P: "creates a ring of energy around them. Exiting that ring empowers Akali's next Attack")

audit.why: diff TRICKY at 7.5/10 with an Akali carry rating of 8.5/10 sits sensibly against a 52.9% win rate over 1295 games — Tahm Kench is favoured on average but the lane has a real losing tail when she snowballs. The content-layer chart giving her levels 4-6 and returning the lane to Tahm Kench at two items matches the shape of the matchup.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely yours — Tongue Lash's range forces Akali to take a slow every time she steps for a CS, and she has no invisibility to absorb it yet. Spam the auto-Tongue Lash pattern to bank two stacks, then back off before she can five-ring you with her passive. Do not overcommit to a stun on Level 1 since she can just walk out; just abuse the slow to win the CS trade. Levels 2 and 3 look even on paper but feel slightly Akali-leaning in practice because Twilight Shroud is now live and absorbs your Q cooldown if she uses it pre-emptively — treat every short trade as stack-fishing and only commit your full Q-stun-Devour pattern when her W is visibly on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely yours — Tongue Lash's 900 range forces Akali to take a slow every time she steps for a CS, and she has no invisibility to absorb it yet. Her Five Point Strike costs 110 energy at rank 1, so she cannot answer more than twice. Bank two stacks with lash-plus-auto, then step clear of Assassin's Mark's ring before she can empower an attack on you. Levels 2 and 3 look even on paper but lean Akali in practice because Twilight Shroud is now live and blanks a committed pattern if she pre-empts it — treat every short trade as stack-fishing and only spend your three stacks when her W is visibly on cooldown.

edits.before: Levels 4 and 5 are Akali's window: her Shroud resets frequently, her E Shuriken Flip closes distance from unpredictable angles, and she can poke you below the grey-health healing threshold before you land three stacks. Farm tight to your tower, let Thick Skin passively bank grey health, and only hit E to shield when she commits a full combo — not to win the trade, but to survive it. Level 6 is when Perfect Execution arrives and she becomes a genuine threat: her R1 knocks you airborne from range, she W-vanishes to dodge your Devour, then R2 executes. Play this window reactively — keep Devour on a hair trigger and swallow her mid-R2 animation if she re-enters to finish; that removes her from the fight entirely and wastes both charges.
edits.after: Levels 4 and 5 are Akali's window: Twilight Shroud is back every 20s at rank 1, her E Shuriken Flip closes distance from unpredictable angles, and she can poke you below the grey-health healing threshold before you land three stacks. Farm tight to your tower, let Thick Skin passively bank grey health, and only hit E to shield after her damage has landed — an empty bank converts into nothing. Level 6 is when Perfect Execution arrives: R1 leaps to you from 675 range and does not knock you up, so the leap itself is the tell, then R2 executes. Shroud makes her unselectable, so Devour will not even cast while she sits inside it — hold your three stacks for the moment she steps out to finish you, and eat her then.

edits.before: At Heartsteel plus Warmog's you near-unkillably regen through her burst windows, and a stacked Q-stun into Devour removes her from any skirmish for long enough that your team collapses.
edits.after: At Heartsteel plus Warmog's you near-unkillably regen through her burst windows, and three stacks spent on Devour — not on the Q stun — removes her from a skirmish long enough for your team to collapse.

edits.after: Stack An Acquired Taste to 3 in short poke exchanges, then spend them on Devour once Twilight Shroud is down

Great trade: Akali wastes Twilight Shroud — commit the full pattern immediately. Bad trade: Q-ing with zero stacks — no stun means you spat at him and donated the trade window.

Great trade: Akali wastes Twilight Shroud — commit the full pattern immediately. Bad trade: Q-ing a target already on 3 stacks you meant to eat — the stun consumes all three and Devour greys out.

notes:
Akali is the one matchup in this slice where the stack-spending choice is forced rather than preferential: Twilight Shroud makes her unable to be selected by spells, so Devour is uncastable while she is inside it. The old text sold "Q-stun into Devour" as the answer to her all-in, which is wrong twice — the combo cannot exist, and the half of it that could exist does not work through W.

The full layer for this matchup still refers to Akali as "him"/"his" in tradeBad, dontsFull[0].d, dontsFull[2].d and breakdown.late ("Devour deletes him"). I fixed the pronouns only in the strings I was already editing for factual reasons; the rest are cosmetic and I left them alone rather than burn length band on them.
